# Rolling statistics

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

print("=== Rolling Statistics ===\n")

print("Rolling statistics summarize data over a moving window.")
print("""
Uses:
  ✅ Smoothing time series
  ✅ Identifying trends
  ✅ Detecting changes
  ✅ Removing noise
""")

np.random.seed(42)

# Create time series data
dates = pd.date_range('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31', freq='D')
n = len(dates)

# Data with trend and noise
value = 50 + 0.02 * np.arange(n) + np.random.normal(0, 5, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({'Date': dates, 'Value': value})

print(f"Data shape: {df.shape}")
print(df.head())

print("\n=== Rolling Mean ===\n")

# Different window sizes
windows = [7, 30, 90]

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

plt.subplot(3, 1, 1)
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
df['Rolling_7'] = df['Value'].rolling(7).mean()
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_7'], label='7-day mean')
plt.title('7-day Rolling Mean')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.subplot(3, 1, 2)
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
df['Rolling_30'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).mean()
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_30'], label='30-day mean')
plt.title('30-day Rolling Mean')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.subplot(3, 1, 3)
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
df['Rolling_90'] = df['Value'].rolling(90).mean()
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_90'], label='90-day mean')
plt.title('90-day Rolling Mean')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rolling Standard Deviation ===\n")

# Rolling std (volatility)
df['Rolling_Std_30'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).std()

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_Std_30'], label='30-day volatility')
plt.title('Rolling Standard Deviation')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Standard Deviation')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rolling Min and Max ===\n")

# Rolling min and max
df['Rolling_Min'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).min()
df['Rolling_Max'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).max()

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.fill_between(df['Date'], df['Rolling_Min'], df['Rolling_Max'], 
                 alpha=0.3, label='30-day range')
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
plt.title('Rolling Min and Max')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rolling Correlation ===\n")

# Create second time series
value2 = 50 + 0.03 * np.arange(n) + np.random.normal(0, 3, n)
df['Value2'] = value2

# Rolling correlation
df['Rolling_Corr'] = df['Value'].rolling(30).corr(df['Value2'])

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Rolling_Corr'])
plt.title('Rolling Correlation (30-day window)')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Correlation')
plt.axhline(y=0, color='black', linestyle='-', alpha=0.3)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Window Options ===\n")

print("Window functions:")
print("  rolling(window): Standard rolling window")
print("  expanding(): Expanding from start")
print("  ewm(): Exponential weighted moving")

# Expanding mean
df['Expanding_Mean'] = df['Value'].expanding().mean()

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Value'], alpha=0.5, label='Original')
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Expanding_Mean'], label='Expanding mean')
plt.title('Expanding Mean')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Rolling Statistics Checklist ===\n")

print("Uses of rolling statistics:")
print("  ✅ Smoothing: Remove noise")
print("  ✅ Trend detection: Reveal direction")
print("  ✅ Volatility: Measure variation")
print("  ✅ Range: Identify extremes")
print("  ✅ Correlation: Track relationships over time")

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **Rolling statistics smooth time series data.**

**Window functions:**
```python
# Rolling window (fixed size)
df['rolling_mean'] = df['value'].rolling(window=7).mean()

# Expanding window (all past data)
df['expanding_mean'] = df['value'].expanding().mean()

# Exponential weighted
df['ewm_mean'] = df['value'].ewm(span=30).mean()
```

**Common rolling statistics:**
```python
# Mean (smoothing)
df['rolling_mean'] = df['value'].rolling(30).mean()

# Standard deviation (volatility)
df['rolling_std'] = df['value'].rolling(30).std()

# Min/Max (range)
df['rolling_min'] = df['value'].rolling(30).min()
df['rolling_max'] = df['value'].rolling(30).max()

# Correlation
df['rolling_corr'] = df['x'].rolling(30).corr(df['y'])

# Count (number of observations)
df['rolling_count'] = df['value'].rolling(30).count()
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Rolling statistics reveal patterns that are hidden in noisy data."
